title: Repeat customers report
summary: Aggregate paid orders per customer and keep only those who came back.
prompt: Marketing wants the customers who ordered **at least twice**. Cancelled orders do not count for anything.
Return `name`, `paid_orders` (number of paid orders), `spent_cents` (their total) and `first_order`
(the date of their first **paid** order), for customers with 2 or more paid orders.
Tables: `customers(id, name)`, `orders(id, customer_id, placed_on, total_cents, status)` where
setup: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), placed_on TEXT NOT NULL,
total_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL);
solution: JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
wrong: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS paid_orders, SUM(o.total_cents) AS spent_cents, MIN(o.placed_on) AS first_order
FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'paid' THEN o.total_cents ELSE 0 END) AS spent_cents,
FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS paid_orders, SUM(o.total_cents) AS spent_cents, MIN(o.placed_on) AS first_order
FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
hints: Filter out cancelled orders in `WHERE`, before grouping, so they cannot affect any column.
`GROUP BY c.id`, then `HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2` filters on the group.
Two customers can spend the same amount: the second sort key decides their order.
